raw_response:
I will keep my full 9.0 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the system I know best, it fits my land and irrigation conditions, and after 40 years I trust stable output more than trying something new. Since my farm is small and some family labor is off-farm, I will keep management simple, timely, and practical: I will use better seed, put most fertilizer where it pays, irrigate when the crop is most sensitive, and avoid excessive field operations. For wheat, I will focus on steady tillering, overwintering, and grain filling with moderate fertilizer and three irrigations because wheat on my land responds well to water. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, feed it a bit more nitrogen, and rely on one main irrigation plus timely pest control because summer rainfall helps but I still have the well as backup. I will use rotary tillage for both crops because it is efficient for my scale and easier for me to manage. My goal is steady yield and controlled costs, not chasing the absolute highest output.
